A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Embodied-IQA work. Their complete main text, Appendices A-I, equations, figures, tables, and references support reliable comparison despite the title change.

before.justification: v1 reports original IQA benchmark results, database analyses, and 1,500 real-world robot experiments, including Tables 2 and 4 and Figure 8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, database-analysis, and real-world robot results, including the appendix Cognition experiments.

M1.justification: The perception-cognition-decision-execution pipeline, VLM/VLA annotation and scoring rules, and robot execution procedure are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B-D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Embodied-IQA images, manipulation tasks, distortion categories, real/simulated scenes, and first-/third-person perspectives. LIVE and TID2013 cross-database evaluations are also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain the same 15 IQA methods across zero-shot, full-reference, and no-reference groups. Figure 8(a) retains the same ten trained comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the 29,520/7,380 split, SRCC/KRCC/PLCC metrics, and 50-epoch training at learning rate 10^-5. Subgroup evaluations, cross-database testing, real-robot procedures, and Appendix F settings also match.

E4.justification: The model correlations, distortion sensitivity and JND analyses, category distributions, real-world cases, and supplementary feature distributions and case studies are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices F-H.

E5.justification: Both versions state that partitioning, training, and testing are repeated ten times and report mean results in Section 5.1. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout, including Tables 2 and 4. For example, TOPIQ-FR's Decision Position SRCC remains 0.7748, while Figure 8 retains real-world correlations of 0.448 for VLM and 0.671 for VLA.

T1.justification: The task and score definitions, kinematic assumptions, and forward/inverse kinematics derivations remain unchanged, including equations (1)-(18) in Appendices C-D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same pipeline, database, and experimental contributions and the need for better embodied IQA metrics. Replacing 'Perceptual' with 'Image' in the title does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of human, machine, and robot preference differences are retained. Appendix A preserves the same limitations concerning vision-only perception, robotic-arm execution, and the relatively small real-world dataset.

D1.justification: The first-page project hyperlink is corrected: its embedded destination changes from Q-Future/CMC-Bench to lcysyzxdxc/EmbodiedIQA, matching the unchanged displayed address. Implementation details, hardware, annotation instructions, and Appendix I's staged noncommercial release statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the database positioning in Table 1, and all 69 numbered references are retained. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Perceptual Quality Assessment for Embodied AI' to 'Image Quality Assessment for Embodied AI,' and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Body wording and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-14 and Tables 1-4 retain their content, captions, visual encodings, numbering, and page placement. There is no figure/table redesign or substantive layout change.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the misleading project-page hyperlink so its destination matches the displayed EmbodiedIQA address, providing a limited improvement in access guidance and document usability. The title edit leaves the scientific substance unchanged: experiments, results, derivations, and limitations are retained. The local PDFs establish the hyperlink correction, not the destination's online availability.
